forms.detail: INN buprenorphine (WHO ATC N07BC01 and N02AE01; INCB lists 'Buprenorphine — Buprénorphine — Buprenorfina'). Chemical name (DEA Diversion Control Division): (2S)-2-[(5R,6R,7R,14S)-17-cyclopropylmethyl-4,5-epoxy-6,14-ethano-3-hydroxy-6-methoxymorphinan-7-yl]-3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. CAS 52485-79-7 (DEA Diversion; NIST). Formula C29H41NO4 and molar mass 467.6401 (NIST, read twice). Other names (NIST): Temgesic, RX 6029M.

DEA Diversion: oral concentrate, oral solution, tablets, injectable liquid and powder for prescription compounding (Methadose, Dolophine). The DEA fact sheet also lists dispersible tablets. EUDA: methadone is the most commonly prescribed medication in opioid agonist treatment in Europe.
The WHO ATC index lists levomethadone (N07BC05) beside methadone.

DEA Diversion (United States): Buprenex (injectable), Belbuca (buccal film), Butrans (transdermal patch), Subutex, Suboxone (sublingual film, with naloxone), Zubsolv (sublingual tablet, with naloxone), Brixadi and Sublocade (extended-release injectable solutions). EUDA (Europe): newer preparations include a prolonged-release solution for injection and a subcutaneous implant. WHO ATC: 'buprenorphine, combinations' (N07BC51).
